Title: The open-source database and workspace for your AI agents.
# The Base for AgentsThe Base for Agents. An open-source database and workspace for AI agents. What they produce stays as data, docs, skills, and apps your team can reuse. Nine posts are in the Content base. The price is $6.50, taken from the Products base. Q&A and product facts — agents draft the reply, a person approves it. Decisions, meeting notes, and context the next agent can read. ## Keep your AI work in the company, not in chat histories. Your team already uses AI, and the work gets done — but it scatters across personal chat windows and leaves when people do. Busabase keeps it as data, docs, skills, and apps the whole company can reuse. The work sits in personal chat windows, and leaves when people do. It lands in one workspace, and stays after people leave. They land in tables, docs, and apps you can open tomorrow. The work stays with the company. Data · Knowledge · Apps · Skills · Playbooks · External Agents. ## One workspace for people and agents. What agents write, the rules they follow, and the agents themselves — all in one workspace. ### Data Base. A Busabase base: posts in a typed table. Your internal tools in one place, built on the same data, so every screen shows the latest version. Save a workflow once as a skill, and any agent can run it next time. Talk to a connected agent right inside Busabase, or connect 40+ external agents over Agent Skills, MCP, and more — Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw. The next agent, a teammate, or an AirApp reads the same data — nobody starts from zero. The same engine runs on your laptop, on your own server, or in Busabase Cloud. Yes. Busabase is open source (MIT): Busabase Desktop keeps data in a folder on your machine, and the Docker image runs on your own server inside your network. Busabase is where agent work lands: typed data, docs, skills, and apps that every agent reads and writes through the same structure, with a history of every change. Yes. With the local engine your data never leaves your machine; on Cloud it stays in your own space.

results.content:
Title: Ambiguous Workspace: 18 productivity apps built for AI agents and humans | Product Hunt
# Ambiguous Workspace. ## 18 productivity apps built for AI agents and humans. Ever ask your AI agent to do something and it says “I don’t have access”? 🙃 Most of the apps where work happens weren’t built for agents, so they either get stuck or end up borrowing your login. That's why we're excited to launch Ambiguous Workspace: 18 productivity apps reimagined so work flows between your team and agents. They include Docs, Mail, Chat, Sheets, CRM, and more. Each agent has its own identity. You can send it an email, message it, assign it a task, or mention it in a comment. Hi Product Hunt, I'm Dan, one of the founders of Ambiguous. This past spring, we had just launched our AI coworkers, with real identities and their own Google and Slack accounts, and Google invited us to the Partner Summit keynote at Cloud Next. We were sitting up front when our Ambiguous AI logo came up on the big screen. At that exact moment, our teammates were texting us that our AI coworkers were getting throttled by Google Workspace. That's when it clicked: every AI agent doing real work was going to hit the same wall. So we built our own workspace, one that treats agents as first-class citizens, and moved our whole team, humans and AI, onto it. Today Ambiguous is 18 productivity apps reimagined so work flows between your team and agents, including Docs, Mail, Chat, Sheets, CRM and Calendar. Bring the agent you already have, and it gets its own identity, not your login. It works in the same apps as your team, and email it sends outside the workspace waits for your OK by default. Our own product marketing agent, Neo, manages our ad campaigns in Ambiguous. Neo builds the sheets that track ad results, maps our campaigns on a Canvas board, writes our launch docs and review decks, and emails us when something needs a decision. All 18 productivity apps, free, for up to 5 teammates. What's the first job you'd hand your agent once it has its own workspace? No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Ambiguous Workspace.

results.title: AgentGrid.io: Shared workspace for humans and agents | Product Hunt
results.content:
What do you think? …

Avishay Cohen

Hey PH 👋

Avishay here, co-founder of Anima, makers of AgentGrid.io.  
Today, we're launching AgentGrid.io, a shared drive for humans and AI agents to collaborate on documents, websites, apps, and designs. Feels like Google Drive for humans, Git for agents.  
  
Bring your own AI agents. Keep your work independent of any AI provider.   
Everyone works on the same live artifacts.

What you can do with AgentGrid:

Collaborate on documents - Google Docs-like multiplayer editing for humans, with a Markdown and Git interface for agents.

Share/publish websites and apps - HTML/React apps are a new type of document - reports, slides, designs, internal apps - Share them securely or publish to the web, simply by asking your chat/agent. [...] Multi-agent-human collab - Let Claude create a report, ChatGPT improve it, Grok Bot generate visuals, and a teammate edit it manually. All on the same artifact.

Share AI work securely - Give every document, report, app, or design a persistent link and structured storage, instead of leaving it buried in a chat.

Version history and control - See who changed what, restore previous versions, and control what each agent can access or modify.

Agent-agnostic, made for all agents - Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Grok Bot, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw, and others via MCP, CLI, and APIs.

Bring your existing work - Import files, websites, and Figma designs to continue working with your agents. You can also ask your agents to simply put their work on AgentGrid.io.

Who it's for: [...] We'll be here all day. Ask anything, share feedback, questions, and thoughts 👇
